analysis.title: Something is breaking beneath the US housing market
key_insights: XHB has traded in a large range since 2024. The latest bounce started near the lower end of the range, and the technical picture is weak. Support could give way if fundamentals worsen and rates rise.
XHB moves inversely to the US 10-year yield, so higher rates are a headwind for homebuilders.
Homebuilder operating margins have fallen below pre-Covid levels as new-home prices fall while construction, labor and financing costs rise.
Construction input costs (goods and services) are rising about 10-11% annually while median new-home prices are falling, so builders are losing pricing power.
The NAHB buyer traffic index has fallen to 18, its weakest reading since the Covid recession.
Mortgage rates are around 7.3% and affordability remains near historically depressed levels. TS Lombard says cheaper homes alone may not bring buyers back.
Housing inventories are rising while starts and permits weaken. Builders are cutting construction, but the supply of available homes could keep pressure on prices and margins.
TS Lombard sees upside risk to US yields because growth is resilient, inflation pressures persist and Fed communication leans hawkish. Homebuilders have little room for a rates shock.
TS Lombard expresses the bearish housing view as a relative-value trade: long RSP versus short XHB at a 1.75:1 ratio to adjust for volatility differences.
